sentence: This project studies how cannabis affects electronic nicotine delivery systems use in young and emerging adults who use both substances.
This project builds a cancer research center that turns discoveries made in the laboratory into therapeutic approaches.
This project builds hydrogel materials from plasmid DNA that copy the properties of living tissues to study how tissue mechanics affect cell behavior.
This project uses computer modeling to study how viruses and the proteins of their host cells interact.
This project uses ontology methods to standardize and bring together behavioral and social science data about Alzheimer's disease.
This project tests whether correcting a common biochemical consequence of mitochondrial diseases with an enzyme tool has therapeutic benefits.
This project builds imaging tools that show the structures and dynamics of proteins and RNAs inside living cells with little photobleaching.
This project builds a two-photon fiberscopy imaging tool that shows how brain regions connect in freely-moving animals such as rodents.
This project tries to find out why aggressive breast cancers resist radiation therapy, focusing on a receptor for vascular endothelial growth factor.
This project tries to find out what causes multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children and how to tell who is at risk of the disease.
This project tries to find out why patients with Merkel cell carcinoma, a skin cancer, fail to respond to blockade therapy.
This project studies how macrophages make and release short non-coding RNAs that switch on immune defense against microbial infections.
This project builds tools that help people explore genome data on the web, using machine learning.
This project builds machine learning and statistical methods that infer causal mechanisms in single-cell morphological profiling and large-scale virtual screening for pharmacology.
This project studies what raises the risk of cancer and how it progresses, looking at genetic, environmental and lifestyle factors.
This project tries to find out why patients with HIV-1 infection lose immune balance, with the goal of a cure.
This project studies how the immune system works in malignant disease and looks for ways to use immunotherapy to treat patients with cancer.
This project keeps high-containment research facilities running so that scientists can develop vaccines and diagnostics against biological threats.
This project uses patient-specific pluripotent stem cells to model interstitial lung diseases and pulmonary fibrosis and to understand what causes them.
This project builds a technology that extracts DNA from resilient microbes so that disease can be detected earlier.
